vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: baoyu-post-to-weibo
Version: 1.103.0

The skill bundle automates Weibo posting using Chrome CDP and high-risk system-level interactions, including keystroke simulation (via AppleScript, PowerShell, and xdotool in `paste-from-clipboard.ts`), clipboard manipulation (using temporary Swift scripts and PowerShell in `copy-to-clipboard.ts`), and process management (`pkill` in `weibo-utils.ts`). While these capabilities are functionally aligned with the goal of bypassing anti-bot detection, they provide a significant attack surface for potential abuse. Additionally, `SKILL.md` contains instructions for the AI agent to automatically kill processes and retry commands without user intervention, and the Markdown renderer (`baoyu-md`) fetches resources from external endpoints like `plantuml.com` and a third-party CDN (`cdn-doocs.oss-cn-shenzhen.aliyuncs.com`). No explicit evidence of data exfiltration or intentional malice was found, but the combination of these powerful automation techniques is inherently risky.

llm.summary: The skill's files, runtime instructions, and requirements line up with its stated purpose (automating Weibo posts via a real Chrome session), but it will access your Chrome profile, clipboard, and send real paste keystrokes — review and run only if you trust the code and the environment.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (post to Weibo via Chrome CDP) matches the shipped scripts and vendor libraries: there are scripts for regular posts and headline articles, a markdown-to-html pipeline, and a Chrome/CDP helper. Requiring a real Chrome profile and using clipboard/paste utilities is coherent for automating browser-based posting and bypassing anti-bot detection.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to execute local TypeScript scripts (via bun or npx) located in scripts/, read optional EXTEND.md config files (project/user/xdg), open or reuse a Chrome profile, copy images/HTML to the system clipboard, and send real paste keystrokes to the frontmost application. These actions are within the posting scope but expand privileges (reading user config, accessing Chrome user-data dirs, manipulating clipboard and sending keystrokes) and thus should be consciously allowed by the user.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no remote install spec — the skill is instruction-only but includes local source files. Execution relies on local runtimes (bun or npx). All code and vendor packages are bundled in the skill (no external download URLs in the provided manifest), which reduces supply-chain download risk compared to a remote install.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials, and that is consistent. However the chrome/CDP helper reads standard environment-driven paths (XDG_DATA_HOME, APPDATA) and inspects Chrome user-data dirs (DevToolsActivePort) to reuse sessions — this gives the scripts access to your browser profile (cookies, saved sessions). Access is proportionate for re-using a logged-in Weibo session, but it's sensitive and worth explicit user approval.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not force-included (always: false) and does not request system-wide changes. It does not declare persistent privileges or attempt to modify other skills. It will reuse local Chrome profiles and may write/read temporary files (images, HTML) in temp dirs as part of normal operation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it says: it runs local scripts (via bun/npx) to control a real Chrome session and post to Weibo. Important things to consider before installing or invoking it:
- It will access your Chrome user-data directories (to reuse or launch a Chrome profile). That means it can act using your logged-in browser session — if you don't want that, use a dedicated/throwaway Chrome profile.
- It manipulates the system clipboard and sends real paste keystrokes (Cmd/Ctrl+V) to the frontmost app. Make sure the correct browser window is frontmost and don't run in contexts where unwanted apps might receive keystrokes.
- There are no remote download URLs in the manifest, but the scripts will be executed locally. Inspect the included scripts if you need higher assurance.
- If you have any doubt, run the scripts manually in a controlled environment (separate Chrome profile, sandbox, or VM) and verify behavior before granting the skill autonomous invocation.
